Virus infection causes diffusion of pigments from the seed hilum, resulting in mottling of the seed coat. Hilum color determines the color and intensity of seed coat discoloration.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':

Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. Diaporthe complex (stem canker), Fusarium root rot and wilt, Pythium seedling blight and root rot, Rhizoctonia seedling blight and root rot, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Charcoal rot, Herbicide injury, Early season frost damage, Insect and mite injury

Seeds may be symptomless or have pink to purple spots extending from the hilum. Crop value may be lowered by dockage or seed certification denial, but yield is not reduced.. Pink to purple spots extending from the hilum on the seed coat; seeds may also be completely symptomless.

Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus: Bean Pod Mottle Virus causes a diffuse mottling pattern across the seed coat due to pigment diffusion from the hilum, with color and intensity varying based on hilum color.
Decision rule  : IF the seed shows discrete, localized pink-to-purple spots extending from the hilum (or no symptoms at all), classify as Purple Seed Stain (A); IF the seed shows a diffuse, spread-out mottling pattern across the seed coat with variable color tied to hilum pigmentation, classify as Bean Pod Mottle Virus (B).
